# Feature: Deterministic Three.js Fixture

<!-- auto-generated by /implement on 2026-08-13 — issue #17 -->

## Intent
Without a controlled app, tests are flaky. `fixtures/web-threejs` is a small deterministic app where draw calls, allocations, textures, or long tasks can be toggled — the benchmark that detection and quick scan become real (T-001, T-004).

## Preconditions
- `fixtures/web-threejs` exists (#12)

## Happy Path
- [x] Fixture starts with documented command without external requests
- [x] At least one toggleable problem (extra draw calls or long task) is activatable via flag/query
- [x] README in fixtures/web-threejs explains why the app exists
- [x] Touched files: zero type escape hatches (typed-strict / Boy Scout)

## Edge Cases
- [x] Fixture starts without network assets (offline)
- [x] Unknown problem param falls back to baseline

## Regression
- [x] Existing packages and `pnpm checks` stay green
- [x] Scope: `fixtures/web-threejs/**`

## Assumptions
- Query param toggle is sufficient for MVP
- No network assets
- Vite dev server is available

## Security Coverage
- No eval/exec; no network requests; no secrets

Not applicable.

## Implementation Notes
- `fixtures/web-threejs/src/main.tsx` reads `?problem=` and applies drawcalls/longtask/alloc.
- Overlay shows active problem.
- README documents usage and offline behavior.
- All 49 tests pass; `pnpm checks` is green.
